qs.stem: The number of ways, in which 16 oranges can be distributed to four children such that each child gets at least one orange, is :
steps: Give each child one orange first; 12 oranges remain to be shared among 4 children with no restriction.
Number of non-negative solutions of x<sub>1</sub>+x<sub>2</sub>+x<sub>3</sub>+x<sub>4</sub> = 12 is <sup>15</sup>C<sub>3</sub>.

qs.stem:
Let A = {0, 1, 2, ......, 9}. Let R be a relation on A defined by (x, y) ∈ R if and only if |x − y| is a multiple of 3. Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : n(R) = 36.
Statement-II : R is an equivalence relation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: x R y exactly when x and y leave the same remainder mod 3. Residue classes in A: remainder 0 has {0,3,6,9} (4 elements), remainder 1 has {1,4,7} (3), remainder 2 has {2,5,8} (3).
n(R) = 4<sup>2</sup> + 3<sup>2</sup> + 3<sup>2</sup> = 16 + 9 + 9 = 34, not 36, so Statement I is incorrect.
Congruence mod 3 is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so R is an equivalence relation: Statement II is correct.
opts: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

qs.stem: The sum of all the real solutions of the equation log<sub>(x+3)</sub>(6x<sup>2</sup> + 28x + 30) = 5 − 2 log<sub>(6x+10)</sub>(x<sup>2</sup> + 6x + 9) is equal to :
steps: Factor: 6x<sup>2</sup>+28x+30 = (6x+10)(x+3), and x<sup>2</sup>+6x+9 = (x+3)<sup>2</sup>. The LHS becomes 1 + log<sub>(x+3)</sub>(6x+10), the RHS becomes 5 − 4 log<sub>(6x+10)</sub>(x+3).
Put t = log<sub>(6x+10)</sub>(x+3): 1 + 1/t = 5 − 4t, so 4t<sup>2</sup> − 4t + 1 = 0, i.e. (2t − 1)<sup>2</sup> = 0 and t = 1/2.
Then x+3 = √(6x+10), so x<sup>2</sup>+6x+9 = 6x+10, x<sup>2</sup> = 1, x = ±1. Both give valid bases (x=1: 4 and 16; x=-1: 2 and 4).
Sum of solutions = 1 + (−1) = 0.

qs.stem: Let π/2 < θ < π and cot θ = −1/(2√2). Then the value of sin(15θ/2)(cos 8θ + sin 8θ) + cos(15θ/2)(cos 8θ − sin 8θ) is equal to :
steps: Expand: sin(15θ/2)cos 8θ − cos(15θ/2)sin 8θ + sin(15θ/2)sin 8θ + cos(15θ/2)cos 8θ = sin(15θ/2 − 8θ) + cos(15θ/2 − 8θ) = −sin(θ/2) + cos(θ/2).
tan θ = −2√2. With t = tan(θ/2): 2t/(1 − t<sup>2</sup>) = −2√2, giving √2 t<sup>2</sup> − t − √2 = 0, so t = √2 or t = −1/√2.
Since θ/2 lies in (π/4, π/2), t > 1, so t = √2. Then sin(θ/2) = √2/√3 and cos(θ/2) = 1/√3.
Value = (1 − √2)/(√3).

qs.stem: Let a, b, c be three vectors such that a × b = 2(a × c). If |a| = 1, |b| = 4, |c| = 2, and the angle between b and c is 60°, then |a · c| is equal to :
steps: a × (b − 2c) = 0, so a = λ(b − 2c) for some scalar λ.
b·c = 4 × 2 × (1/2) = 4. Then |a|2 = λ2(16 + 16 − 4(4)) = 16λ2 = 1, so λ = ±1/4.
a·c = λ(b·c − 2|c|2) = λ(4 − 8) = −4λ = −1 or 1, so |a·c| = 1.

qs.stem: Let I(x) = ∫ 3dx / ((4x + 6)√(4x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 3)) and I(0) = (√3)/(4) + 20. If I(1/2) = (a√2)/(b) + c, where a, b, c ∈ N, gcd(a, b) = 1, then a + b + c is equal to :
steps: Note 4x<sup>2</sup>+8x+3 = (2x+1)(2x+3). Claim: I(x) = (3/4)√((4x+2)/(4x+6)) + C. Check: derivative of √((4x+2)/(4x+6)) is 8/((4x+6)<sup>3/2</sup>(4x+2)<sup>1/2</sup>), and multiplying by 3/4 gives 3/((4x+6)√(4x<sup>2</sup>+8x+3)). Good.

qs.stem: Let ∑<sub>k=1</sub><sup>n</sup> a<sub>k</sub> = αn<sup>2</sup> + βn. If a<sub>10</sub> = 59 and a<sub>6</sub> = 7a<sub>1</sub>, then α + β is equal to :
steps: a<sub>n</sub> = S<sub>n</sub> − S<sub>n−1</sub> = α(2n − 1) + β. So a<sub>1</sub> = α + β, a<sub>6</sub> = 11α + β, a<sub>10</sub> = 19α + β.
a<sub>6</sub> = 7a<sub>1</sub>: 11α + β = 7α + 7β, so 4α = 6β and α = 3β/2.
α + β = 5.

qs.stem: Bag A contains 9 white and 8 black balls, while bag B contains 6 white and 4 black balls. One ball is randomly picked up from the bag B and mixed up with the balls in the bag A. Then a ball is randomly drawn from the bag A. If the probability, that the ball drawn is white, is p/q, gcd(p, q) = 1, then p + q is equal to :
steps: Case 1: white ball moved (prob 6/10); bag A then has 10 white out of 18, so contributes (6/10)(10/18) = 1/3.
Case 2: black ball moved (prob 4/10); bag A then has 9 white out of 18, so contributes (4/10)(9/18) = 1/5.

qs.stem: Consider two sets A = {x ∈ Z : ||x − 3| − 3| ≤ 1} and B = {x ∈ R − {1, 2} : ((x − 2)(x − 4))/(x − 1) log<sub>e</sub>(|x − 2|) = 0}. Then the number of onto functions f : A → B is equal to :
steps: ||x−3|−3| ≤ 1 gives 2 ≤ |x−3| ≤ 4, so x ∈ [−1, 1] ∪ [5, 7]. Integers: −1, 0, 1, 5, 6, 7, so n(A) = 6.
In B the expression vanishes when x = 4 or |x−2| = 1, i.e. x = 3 or x = 1; x = 1 and x = 2 are excluded, so B = {3, 4}, n(B) = 2.
Onto functions from a 6-element set to a 2-element set: 2<sup>6</sup> − 2 = 62.

qs.stem: An equilateral triangle OAB is inscribed in the parabola y<sup>2</sup> = 4x with the vertex O at the vertex of the parabola. Then the minimum distance of the circle having AB as a diameter from the origin is :
steps: By symmetry OA makes 30° with the axis. Take A = (t<sup>2</sup>, 2t): tan 30° = 2t/t<sup>2</sup> = 2/t, so t = 2√3 and A = (12, 4√3), B = (12, −4√3).
Circle on AB as diameter: centre C = (12, 0), radius 4√3.
The origin is outside the circle (OC = 12 > 4√3), so the minimum distance is OC − r = 12 − 4√3 = 4(3 − √3).

qs.stem: Let a = i − 2j + 3k, b = 2i + j − k, c = λi + j + k and v = a × b. If v·c = 11 and the length of the projection of b on c is p, then 9p2 is equal to :
steps: a × b = (2 − 3)i − (−1 − 6)j + (1 + 4)k = −i + 7j + 5k.
v·c = −λ + 7 + 5 = 11, so λ = 1 and c = i + j + k.

qs.stem:
The system of linear equations
x + y + z = 6
2x + 5y + az = 36
x + 2y + 3z = b has :
steps: Eliminating x: (Eq2 − 2Eq1) gives 3y + (a − 2)z = 24 and (Eq3 − Eq1) gives y + 2z = b − 6.
The coefficient determinant equals 8 − a, so for a = 8 the system is not unique. Then 3y + 6z = 24, i.e. y + 2z = 8.
This agrees with y + 2z = b − 6 only when b − 6 = 8, i.e. b = 14, giving infinitely many solutions; for b = 16 there is no solution.
opts: unique solution for a = 8 and b = 16
unique solution for a = 8 and b = 14
infinitely many solutions for a = 8 and b = 14
infinitely many solutions for a = 8 and b = 16

qs.stem: If z = (√3)/(2) + i/2, i = √−1, then (z<sup>201</sup> − i)<sup>8</sup> is equal to :
steps: z = cos(π/6) + i sin(π/6), so z<sup>201</sup> = cos(201π/6) + i sin(201π/6).
(−i − i)<sup>8</sup> = (−2i)<sup>8</sup> = 2<sup>8</sup> i<sup>8</sup> = 256.

qs.stem: The area of the region enclosed between the circles x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = 4 and x<sup>2</sup> + (y − 2)<sup>2</sup> = 4 is :
steps: Subtracting the equations gives y = 1, so the circles meet at x = ±√3.

Between x = −√3 and √3 the region lies under the upper arc y = √(4 − x<sup>2</sup>) of the first circle and above the lower arc y = 2 − √(4 − x<sup>2</sup>) of the second, so A = ∫<sub>−√3</sub><sup>√3</sup> (2√(4 − x<sup>2</sup>) − 2) dx.
∫<sub>−√3</sub><sup>√3</sup> √(4−x<sup>2</sup>) dx = 2[(x/2)√(4−x<sup>2</sup>) + 2 sin<sup>−1</sup>(x/2)] from 0 to √3 = 2(√3/2 + 2π/3) = √3 + 4π/3.
A = 2(√3 + 4π/3) − 4√3 = 8π/3 − 2√3 = (2)/(3)(4π − 3√3).

qs.stem: If the points of intersection of the ellipses x<sup>2</sup> + 2y<sup>2</sup> − 6x − 12y + 23 = 0 and 4x<sup>2</sup> + 2y<sup>2</sup> − 20x − 12y + 35 = 0 lie on a circle of radius r and centre (a, b), then the value of ab + 18r<sup>2</sup> is :
steps: Every curve S<sub>1</sub> + λS<sub>2</sub> = 0 passes through the common points. Requiring equal coefficients of x<sup>2</sup> and y<sup>2</sup>: 1 + 4λ = 2 + 2λ, so λ = 1/2.
The curve becomes 3x<sup>2</sup> + 3y<sup>2</sup> − 16x − 18y + 81/2 = 0, i.e. x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> − (16/3)x − 6y + 27/2 = 0.

qs.stem: If the mean and the variance of the data (Class 4–8, 8–12, 12–16, 16–20 with frequencies 3, λ, 4, 7 respectively) are μ and 19 respectively, then the value of λ + μ is :
steps: Class marks 6, 10, 14, 18. ∑f = 14 + λ, ∑fx = 200 + 10λ, ∑fx<sup>2</sup> = 3160 + 100λ.
Variance condition: (3160 + 100λ)/(14 + λ) − ((200 + 10λ)/(14 + λ))<sup>2</sup> = 19, which is satisfied by λ = 6.
Check: λ = 6 gives μ = 260/20 = 13 and variance 3760/20 − 169 = 188 − 169 = 19.

qs.stem: The least value of (cos<sup>2</sup>θ − 6 sinθ cosθ + 3 sin<sup>2</sup>θ + 2) is :
steps: Use double angles: cos<sup>2</sup>θ = (1 + cos 2θ)/2, sin<sup>2</sup>θ = (1 − cos 2θ)/2, 6 sinθ cosθ = 3 sin 2θ.
Expression = 1/2 + (cos 2θ)/2 − 3 sin 2θ + 3/2 − (3 cos 2θ)/2 + 2 = 4 − cos 2θ − 3 sin 2θ.
cos 2θ + 3 sin 2θ ranges over [−√10, √10], so the minimum is 4 − √10.

qs.stem: If f(x) = (a|x| + x<sup>2</sup> − 2(sin|x|)(cos|x|))/(x) for x ≠ 0 and f(x) = b for x = 0, is continuous at x = 0, then a + b is equal to :
steps: Note 2 sin|x| cos|x| = sin 2|x|. For x > 0: f(x) = (ax + x<sup>2</sup> − sin 2x)/x → a − 2 as x → 0.
For x < 0: |x| = −x, so f(x) = (−ax + x<sup>2</sup> + sin 2x)/x → −a + 2.
Continuity needs the two limits equal: a − 2 = 2 − a, so a = 2, and then b = the common limit = 0.

qs.stem: Let PQ be a chord of the hyperbola x<sup>2</sup>/4 − y<sup>2</sup>/b<sup>2</sup> = 1, perpendicular to the x-axis such that OPQ is an equilateral triangle, O being the centre of the hyperbola. If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is √3, then the area of the triangle OPQ is :
steps: e<sup>2</sup> = 1 + b<sup>2</sup>/4 = 3, so b<sup>2</sup> = 8.
Let P = (x<sub>0</sub>, y<sub>0</sub>) with OP at 30° to the x-axis (triangle equilateral, PQ vertical): y<sub>0</sub> = x<sub>0</sub>/√3.
Substitute: x<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>/4 − x<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>/24 = 1, so (5/24)x<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> = 1 and x<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> = 24/5.
Side = 2y<sub>0</sub>, area = (√3/4)(4x<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>/3) = x<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>/√3 = 24/(5√3) = (8√3)/(5).

qs.stem: Let A(1, 2) and C(−3, −6) be two diagonally opposite vertices of a rhombus, whose sides AD and BC are parallel to the line 7x − y = 14. If B(α, β) and D(γ, δ) are the other two vertices, then |α + β + γ + δ| is equal to :
steps: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, so B + D = A + C = (1 − 3, 2 − 6) = (−2, −4).
Hence α + γ = −2 and β + δ = −4.
|α + β + γ + δ| = |−2 − 4| = 6.

qs.stem: Let S denote the set of 4-digit numbers abcd such that a > b > c > d and P denote the set of 5-digit numbers having product of its digits equal to 20. Then n(S) + n(P) is equal to ______.
steps: Strictly decreasing digits: choose any 4 distinct digits from 0-9 and arrange in decreasing order (leading digit is automatically non-zero), so n(S) = <sup>10</sup>C<sub>4</sub> = 210.
Digits of P are non-zero with product 20: multisets {1,1,1,4,5} and {1,1,2,2,5}.
Arrangements: 5!/3! = 20 and 5!/(2! 2!) = 30, so n(P) = 50.

qs.stem: If the solution curve y = f(x) of the differential equation (x<sup>2</sup> − 4)y′ − 2xy + 2(4 − x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 0, x > 2, passes through the point (3, 15), then the local maximum value of f is ______.
steps: Divide by (x<sup>2</sup>−4): y′ − (2x/(x<sup>2</sup>−4)) y = −2(x<sup>2</sup>−4). Integrating factor = 1/(x<sup>2</sup>−4), so d/dx [y/(x<sup>2</sup>−4)] = −2x.
y/(x<sup>2</sup>−4) = −x<sup>2</sup> + C; at (3, 15): 3 = −9 + C, so C = 12 and f(x) = (x<sup>2</sup>−4)(12 − x<sup>2</sup>).
f′(x) = 4x(8 − x<sup>2</sup>), which changes from + to − at x = 2√2 (in the domain x > 2).
f(2√2) = (8 − 4)(12 − 8) = 16.

qs.stem: Let A = [[0, 2, −3], [−2, 0, 1], [3, −1, 0]] and B be a matrix such that B(I − A) = I + A. Then the sum of the diagonal elements of B<sup>T</sup>B is equal to ______.
steps: A is skew-symmetric (A<sup>T</sup> = −A), and I − A is invertible (its determinant is 15), so B = (I + A)(I − A)<sup>−1</sup>.
B<sup>T</sup> = (I − A)<sup>−T</sup>(I + A)<sup>T</sup> = (I + A)<sup>−1</sup>(I − A). Since (I + A) and (I − A) commute, B<sup>T</sup>B = (I + A)<sup>−1</sup>(I − A)(I + A)(I − A)<sup>−1</sup> = I.
So B is orthogonal and the trace of B<sup>T</sup>B is 3.

qs.stem: The number of elements in the set S = {x : x ∈ [0, 100] and ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> t<sup>2</sup> sin(x − t) dt = x<sup>2</sup>} is ______.
steps: Substitute t → x − t: the integral equals ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> (x − t)<sup>2</sup> sin t dt.
Integrate by parts twice: = x<sup>2</sup> − 2∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> (x − t) cos t dt = x<sup>2</sup> − 2(1 − cos x).
Setting this equal to x<sup>2</sup> gives cos x = 1, so x = 2nπ.
2nπ ≤ 100 gives n ≤ 15.9, so n = 0, 1, ..., 15: 16 elements.

qs.stem: If the image of the point P(a, 2, a) in the line x/2 = (y + a)/1 = z/1 is Q and the image of Q in the line (x − 2b)/2 = (y − a)/1 = (z + 2b)/(−5) is P, then a + b is equal to ______.
steps: Foot R of the perpendicular from P on L<sub>1</sub>: R = (2λ, λ − a, λ) with PR · (2, 1, 1) = 0, giving 3λ = 2a + 1. Then Q = 2R − P = ((5a + 4)/3, (−2a − 4)/3, (a + 2)/3).

Reflection of Q in L<sub>2</sub> is P, so PQ is perpendicular to L<sub>2</sub>: PQ · (2, 1, −5) = 0. PQ = ((4 + 2a)/3, −(2a + 10)/3, (2 − 2a)/3), so 2(4 + 2a) − (2a + 10) − 5(2 − 2a) = 0, i.e. 12a − 12 = 0 and a = 1.

Then Q = (3, −2, 1) and the midpoint of PQ is (2, 0, 1). This must lie on L<sub>2</sub>, which for a = 1 passes through (2b, 1, −2b): (2 − 2b)/2 = (0 − 1)/1 gives 1 − b = −1, so b = 2 (z-ratio (1 + 4)/(−5) = −1 agrees).

qs.stem: The current passing through a conducting loop in the form of equilateral triangle of side 4√3 cm is 2 A. The magnetic field at its centroid is α × 10<sup>−5</sup> T. The value of α is ______. (Given: μ<sub>0</sub> = 4π × 10<sup>−7</sup> SI units)
steps: Distance of centroid from each side (inradius) = a/(2√3) = 4√3/(2√3) = 2 cm = 2 × 10<sup>−2</sup> m.
One side gives B = (μ<sub>0</sub>I)/(4πd)(sin 60° + sin 60°) = (10<sup>−7</sup> × 2)/(2 × 10<sup>−2</sup>) × √3 = √3 × 10<sup>−5</sup> T.
Three sides add in the same direction: B = 3√3 × 10<sup>−5</sup> T, so α = 3√3.

qs.stem: Two short dipoles (A, B), A having charges ± 2 μC and length 1 cm and B having charges ± 4 μC and length 1 cm are placed with their centres 80 cm apart as shown in the figure. The electric field at a point P, equi-distant from the centres of both dipoles is _______ N/C.
steps: Dipole moments: p<sub>B</sub> = 4 × 10<sup>−6</sup> × 10<sup>−2</sup> = 4 × 10<sup>−8</sup> C m, p<sub>A</sub> = 2 × 10<sup>−8</sup> C m. P is 40 cm = 0.4 m from each centre.

P lies on the equatorial line of the vertical dipole B: E<sub>1</sub> = kp<sub>B</sub>/r<sup>3</sup> = 9 × 10<sup>9</sup> × 4 × 10<sup>−8</sup>/0.064 = 5625 N/C. P lies on the axis of the horizontal dipole A: E<sub>2</sub> = 2kp<sub>A</sub>/r<sup>3</sup> = 2 × 9 × 10<sup>9</sup> × 2 × 10<sup>−8</sup>/0.064 = 5625 N/C.
The two fields are perpendicular, so E = √(E<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> + E<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup>) = 5625√2 = (9)/(16)√2 × 10<sup>4</sup> N/C.

qs.stem: Suppose a long solenoid of 100 cm length, radius 2 cm having 500 turns per unit length, carries a current I = 10 sin(ωt) A, where ω = 1000 rad/s. A circular conducting loop (B) of radius 1 cm is coaxially slided through the solenoid at a speed v = 1 cm/s. The r.m.s. current through the loop when the coil B is inserted 10 cm inside the solenoid is (α)/(√2) μA. The value of α is ______. [Resistance of the loop = 10 Ω]
steps: Inside the long solenoid B = μ<sub>0</sub>nI, so flux through the loop is φ = μ<sub>0</sub>n I πr<sup>2</sup> and emf = μ<sub>0</sub>nπr<sup>2</sup> (dI/dt).
Peak emf = μ<sub>0</sub>nπr<sup>2</sup> I<sub>0</sub>ω = 4π × 10<sup>−7</sup> × 500 × π × 10<sup>−4</sup> × 10 × 1000 = 2π<sup>2</sup> × 10<sup>−3</sup> V ≈ 1.974 × 10<sup>−3</sup> V.
Peak current = emf/R = 1.974 × 10<sup>−4</sup> A ≈ 197 μA; r.m.s. = 197/√2 μA, so α = 197.

qs.stem: A circular loop of radius 7 cm is placed in uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T directed perpendicular to plane of loop. The loop is converted into a square loop in 0.5 s. The EMF induced in the loop is ________ mV.
steps: Same wire length: 2πr = 4ℓ, so side ℓ = πr/2 and square area A<sub>f</sub> = π<sup>2</sup>r<sup>2</sup>/4 = A<sub>i</sub> × (π/4).
Circle area A<sub>i</sub> = πr<sup>2</sup> = 1.539 × 10<sup>−2</sup> m<sup>2</sup>; A<sub>f</sub> = 1.209 × 10<sup>−2</sup> m<sup>2</sup>, so |ΔA| = 3.30 × 10<sup>−3</sup> m<sup>2</sup>.
emf = B|ΔA|/Δt = 0.2 × 3.30 × 10<sup>−3</sup>/0.5 = 1.32 × 10<sup>−3</sup> V = 1.32 mV.

qs.stem: The ratio of speeds of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and a medium, having dielectric constant k = 3 and permeability of μ = 2μ<sub>0</sub>, is (μ<sub>0</sub> = permeability of vacuum)
steps: Speed in a medium v = 1/√(με) and in vacuum c = 1/√(μ<sub>0</sub>ε<sub>0</sub>).
c/v = √(μ<sub>r</sub>ε<sub>r</sub>) = √(2 × 3) = √6, so the ratio is √6 : 1.

qs.stem: A small metallic sphere of diameter 2 mm and density 10.5 g/cm<sup>3</sup> is dropped in glycerine having viscosity 10 Poise and density 1.5 g/cm<sup>3</sup> respectively. The terminal velocity attained by the sphere is ____ cm/s. (π = 22/7 and g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>)
steps: Convert to SI: r = 10<sup>−3</sup> m, ρ − σ = 9000 kg/m<sup>3</sup>, η = 10 P = 1 Pa s.
v<sub>T</sub> = 2r<sup>2</sup>(ρ − σ)g/(9η) = 2 × 10<sup>−6</sup> × 9000 × 10/9 = 0.02 m/s.
So v<sub>T</sub> = 2 cm/s.

qs.stem: One mole of an ideal diatomic gas expands from volume V to 2V isothermally at a temperature 27° C and does W joule of work. If the gas undergoes same magnitude of expansion adiabatically from 27° C doing the same amount of work W, then its final temperature will be (close to) ________ °C. (log<sub>e</sub>2 = 0.693)
steps: Isothermal work W = RT ln 2 = R × 300 × 0.693.
In the adiabatic expansion the same work comes from internal energy: C<sub>v</sub>ΔT = −W with C<sub>v</sub> = 5R/2.
ΔT = −(2/5)(300)(0.693) = −83.2 K, so final temperature = 27 − 83.2 ≈ −56 °C.

qs.stem: Two charges 7 μC and −2 μC are placed at (−9, 0, 0) cm and (9, 0, 0) cm respectively in an external field E = (A)/(r2) r̂, where A = 9 × 105 N/C.m2. Considering the potential at infinity is 0, the electrostatic energy of the configuration is ________J.
steps: The field kq/r<sup>2</sup> with kq = 9 × 10<sup>5</sup> corresponds to a point charge q = 10<sup>−4</sup> C at the origin, 9 cm from each given charge.
Interaction with the source: k(10<sup>−4</sup>)(7 × 10<sup>−6</sup>)/0.09 = 70 J and k(10<sup>−4</sup>)(−2 × 10<sup>−6</sup>)/0.09 = −20 J.
Mutual energy of the two charges: k(7 × 10<sup>−6</sup>)(−2 × 10<sup>−6</sup>)/0.18 = −0.7 J. Total = 70 − 20 − 0.7 = 49.3 J.

qs.stem: Which of the following pair of nuclei are isobars of the element ?
steps: Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic number.
Only <sup>3</sup><sub>1</sub>H and <sup>3</sup><sub>2</sub>He share A = 3 with Z = 1 and 2. The others differ in A (isotopes in options 3 and 4).

qs.stem: A paratrooper jumps from an aeroplane and opens a parachute after 2 s of free fall and starts deaccelerating with 3 m/s<sup>2</sup>. At 10 m height from ground, while descending with the help of parachute, the speed of paratrooper is 5 m/s. The initial height of the airplane is ________m. (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>)
steps: Free fall for 2 s: h<sub>1</sub> = (1/2)(10)(4) = 20 m and speed v = 20 m/s.
Deceleration phase: 5<sup>2</sup> = 20<sup>2</sup> − 2(3)h<sub>2</sub>, so h<sub>2</sub> = 375/6 = 62.5 m.
Initial height = h<sub>1</sub> + h<sub>2</sub> + 10 = 20 + 62.5 + 10 = 92.5 m.

qs.stem: A body of mass 14 kg initially at rest explodes and breaks into three fragments of masses in the ratio 2 : 2 : 3. The two pieces of equal masses fly off perpendicular to each other with a speed of 18 m/s each. The velocity of the heavier fragment is ________ m/s.
steps: Masses: 14 kg split in ratio 2:2:3 gives 4 kg, 4 kg and 6 kg.
Momenta of the two equal pieces: 4 × 18 = 72 kg m/s each, perpendicular, so resultant = 72√2.
By momentum conservation the heavy piece carries equal and opposite momentum: 6v = 72√2, so v = 12√2 m/s.

qs.stem: For the given logic gate circuit, which of the following is the correct truth table? (Input n goes directly to one input of a NAND gate and also to an OR gate; input m goes to the other input of the OR gate; the OR output feeds the second input of the NAND gate; output z is the NAND output.)
steps: The OR gate outputs n + m, and the NAND gate gets n and (n + m), so z = NOT[n · (n + m)].
By absorption n · (n + m) = n, so z = NOT n.
Hence z = 1 when n = 0 (both m values) and z = 0 when n = 1, which is the first table.

qs.stem: An air bubble of volume 2.9 cm<sup>3</sup> rises from the bottom of a swimming pool of 5 m deep. At the bottom of the pool water temperature is 17 °C. The volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface, where the water temperature is 27 °C, is ________ cm<sup>3</sup>. (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>, density of water = 10<sup>3</sup> kg/m<sup>3</sup>, and 1 atm pressure is 10<sup>5</sup> Pa)
steps: Pressure at bottom P<sub>1</sub> = 10<sup>5</sup> + 10<sup>3</sup> × 10 × 5 = 1.5 × 10<sup>5</sup> Pa, T<sub>1</sub> = 290 K; at surface P<sub>2</sub> = 10<sup>5</sup> Pa, T<sub>2</sub> = 300 K.
P<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub>/T<sub>1</sub> = P<sub>2</sub>V<sub>2</sub>/T<sub>2</sub> gives V<sub>2</sub> = 1.5 × 2.9 × (300/290) = 4.5 cm<sup>3</sup>.

qs.stem: The internal energy of a monotomic gas is 3nRT. One mole of helium is kept in a cylinder having internal cross section area of 17 cm<sup>2</sup> and fitted with a light movable frictionless piston. The gas is heated slowly by supplying 126 J heat. If the temperature rises by 4 °C, then the piston will move ______ cm. (atmospheric pressure = 10<sup>5</sup> Pa)
steps: ΔU = 3nRΔT = 3 × 1 × 8.314 × 4 = 99.8 J.
Work done at constant pressure W = Q − ΔU = 126 − 99.8 = 26.2 J = PΔV.
ΔV = 26.2/10<sup>5</sup> = 2.62 × 10<sup>−4</sup> m<sup>3</sup>, so displacement = ΔV/A = 2.62 × 10<sup>−4</sup>/(17 × 10<sup>−4</sup>) = 0.154 m ≈ 15.4 cm, nearest option 15.5.

qs.stem: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5 mm is charged by a battery. On introducing a mica sheet of 2 mm and maintaining the connections of the plates with the terminals of the battery, it is found that it draws 25% more charge from the battery. The dielectric constant of mica is ________.
steps: The battery stays connected, so Q = CV and 25% more charge means C = 1.25C<sub>0</sub>.
C<sub>0</sub> = ε<sub>0</sub>A/5; with the slab C = ε<sub>0</sub>A/(3 + 2/K) (lengths in mm).

qs.stem: When an unpolarized light falls at a particular angle on a glass plate (placed in air), it is observed that the reflected beam is linearly polarized. The angle of refracted beam with respect to the normal is _____. (tan<sup>−1</sup>(1.52) = 57.7°, refractive indices of air and glass are 1.00 and 1.52, respectively.)
steps: Reflected light is fully polarized at the Brewster angle: tan i<sub>B</sub> = 1.52, so i<sub>B</sub> = 57.7°.
At this angle the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, so r = 90° − 57.7° = 32.3°.

qs.stem: The velocity of sound in air is doubled when the temperature is raised from 0 °C to α °C. The value of α is _______.
steps: Speed of sound v ∝ √T (absolute temperature).
2 = √(T′/273), so T′ = 4 × 273 = 1092 K.
α = 1092 − 273 = 819 °C.

qs.stem: A ball of radius r and density ρ dropped through a viscous liquid of density σ and viscosity η attains its terminal velocity at time t, given by t = A ρ<sup>a</sup> r<sup>b</sup> η<sup>c</sup> σ<sup>d</sup>, where A is a constant and a, b, c and d are integers. The value of (b + c)/(a + d) is ________.
steps: Dimensions: [ρ] = ML<sup>−3</sup>, [r] = L, [η] = ML<sup>−1</sup>T<sup>−1</sup>, [t] = T.
T: −c = 1 gives c = −1. M: a + d + c = 0 gives a + d = 1. L: −3(a + d) + b − c = 0 gives b = 3 − 1 = 2.

qs.stem: The average energy released per fission for the nucleus of <sup>235</sup><sub>92</sub>U is 190 MeV. When all the atoms of 47 g pure <sup>235</sup><sub>92</sub>U undergo fission process, the energy released is α × 10<sup>23</sup> MeV. The value of α is ______. (Avogadro Number = 6 × 10<sup>23</sup> per mole)
steps: Number of moles = 47/235 = 0.2, so number of atoms = 0.2 × 6 × 10<sup>23</sup> = 1.2 × 10<sup>23</sup>.
Energy = 1.2 × 10<sup>23</sup> × 190 MeV = 228 × 10<sup>23</sup> MeV, so α = 228.

qs.stem: The size of the images of an object, formed by a thin lens are equal when the object is placed at two different positions 8 cm and 24 cm from the lens. The focal length of the lens is _______ cm.
steps: Magnification magnitude |m| = f/|u − f|.
Equal sizes at u = 8 and u = 24 with different image natures: f/(f − 8) = f/(24 − f).
So f − 8 = 24 − f, giving f = 16 cm.

qs.stem:
Identify the CORRECT set of details from the following :
A. [Co(NH3)6]3+ : Inner orbital complex; d2sp3 hybridized
B. [MnCl6]3− : Outer orbital complex; sp3d2 hybridized
C. [CoF6]3− : Outer orbital complex; d2sp3 hybridized
D. [FeF6]3− : Outer orbital complex; sp3d2 hybridized
E. [Ni(CN)4]2− : Inner orbital complex; sp3 hybridized
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: A: Co<sup>3+</sup> is d<sup>6</sup>; NH<sub>3</sub> is a strong-field ligand, so electrons pair up and d<sup>2</sup>sp<sup>3</sup> (inner orbital) forms. Correct.

B: Mn<sup>3+</sup> is d<sup>4</sup> with weak-field Cl<sup>−</sup>, so no pairing and sp<sup>3</sup>d<sup>2</sup> (outer orbital). Correct. D: Fe<sup>3+</sup> (d<sup>5</sup>) with weak F<sup>−</sup> is sp<sup>3</sup>d<sup>2</sup>, outer orbital. Correct.

C is wrong because F<sup>−</sup> is weak field, so [CoF<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3−</sup> is sp<sup>3</sup>d<sup>2</sup>, not d<sup>2</sup>sp<sup>3</sup>. E is wrong because Ni<sup>2+</sup> (d<sup>8</sup>) with CN<sup>−</sup> is square planar dsp<sup>2</sup>. Hence A, B, D only.

qs.stem: Both human DNA and RNA are chiral molecules. The chirality in DNA and RNA arised due to the presence of
steps: The sugar in DNA is 2-deoxyribose and in RNA is ribose; both occur in the D-configuration.
The bases are planar and the phosphate group is not a stereocentre, so the chirality comes from the D-sugar unit.

qs.stem: Consider the electrochemical cell shown, where a metal electrode (M) is undergoing redox reaction by forming M<sup>+</sup> (M → M<sup>+</sup> + e<sup>−</sup>). The cation M<sup>+</sup> is present in two different concentrations c<sub>1</sub> and c<sub>2</sub> as shown (two M electrodes in M<sup>+</sup>X<sup>−</sup> solutions of concentration c<sub>2</sub> on the left and c<sub>1</sub> on the right, separated by a semi permeable membrane). Which of the following statement is correct for generating a positive cell potential ?
steps: This is a concentration cell with E° = 0: E = (RT/nF) ln([M<sup>+</sup>]<sub>cathode</sub>/[M<sup>+</sup>]<sub>anode</sub>).
E is positive only when the cathode solution is the more concentrated one.
So if c<sub>1</sub> is at the cathode, c<sub>1</sub> > c<sub>2</sub>; if c<sub>1</sub> is at the anode, c<sub>1</sub> < c<sub>2</sub>. Option (3).
opts: If c<sub>1</sub> is present at anode, then c<sub>1</sub> > c<sub>2</sub>.
If c<sub>1</sub> is present at anode, then c<sub>1</sub> = c<sub>2</sub>.
If c<sub>1</sub> is present at cathode, then c<sub>1</sub> > c<sub>2</sub>.
If c<sub>1</sub> is present at cathode, then c<sub>1</sub> < c<sub>2</sub>.

qs.stem: Elements X and Y belong to Group 15. The difference between the electronegativity values of 'X' and phosphorus is higher than that of the difference between phosphorus and 'Y'. 'X' & 'Y' are respectively
steps: Pauling electronegativities: N 3.0, P 2.1, As 2.0, Sb 1.9, Bi 1.9.
X = N gives |3.0 − 2.1| = 0.9, while Y = As gives |2.1 − 2.0| = 0.1, so the condition holds.
Other options fail: Bi & N gives 0.2 vs 0.9, As & Sb gives 0.1 vs 0.2, As & Bi gives 0.1 vs 0.2.

qs.stem:
Which statements are NOT TRUE about XeO2F2 ?
A. It has a see-saw shape.
B. Xe has 5 electron pairs in its valence shell in XeO2F2.
C. The O–Xe–O bond angle is close to 180°.
D. The F–Xe–F bond angle is close to 180°.
E. Xe has 16 valence electrons in XeO2F2.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: XeO<sub>2</sub>F<sub>2</sub>: 4 bond (sigma) positions plus 1 lone pair, trigonal bipyramidal geometry, see-saw shape, with the lone pair and both Xe=O in the equatorial plane. A is true.
The two axial F atoms give F–Xe–F close to 180° (D true); the O–Xe–O angle is close to 120°, so C is not true.
Counting the two Xe=O pi bonds, Xe has 7 electron pairs (14 electrons, not 16) around it, so B and E are not true. Not true: B, C, E.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The second ionisation enthalpy of Na is larger than the corresponding ionisation enthalpy of Mg.
Statement II : The ionic radius of O2− is larger than that of F−.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
steps: Na<sup>+</sup> has the stable neon configuration, so removing a second electron (from 2p) is very hard: IE<sub>2</sub>(Na) ≈ 4562 kJ/mol versus IE<sub>2</sub>(Mg) ≈ 1451 kJ/mol. Statement I is true.
O<sup>2−</sup> and F<sup>−</sup> are isoelectronic; the lower nuclear charge of O makes O<sup>2−</sup> larger. Statement II is true.
opts: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
Statement I is true but statement II is false.

qs.stem: The oxidation state of chromium in the final product formed in the reaction between KI and acidified K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> solution is
steps: Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sup>2−</sup> + 14H<sup>+</sup> + 6I<sup>−</sup> → 2Cr<sup>3+</sup> + 3I<sub>2</sub> + 7H<sub>2</sub>O.
Dichromate is reduced from +6 to +3 (iodide is oxidised to I<sub>2</sub>), so Cr ends as Cr<sup>3+</sup>.

qs.stem:
It is noticed that Pb2+ is more stable than Pb4+ but Sn2+ is less stable than Sn4+.
Observe the following reactions.
PbO2 + Pb → 2PbO; ΔrG°(1)
SnO2 + Sn → 2SnO; ΔrG°(2)
Identify the correct set from the following.
steps: Reaction (1) converts Pb(IV) and Pb(0) into the more stable Pb(II) (inert pair effect), so it is spontaneous: Δ<sub>r</sub>G°(1) < 0.
Reaction (2) would convert the stable Sn(IV) into the less stable Sn(II), so it is non-spontaneous: Δ<sub>r</sub>G°(2) > 0.

qs.stem: The work function of two metals (M<sub>A</sub> and M<sub>B</sub>) are in the 1 : 2 ratio. When these metals are exposed to photons of energy 6 eV, the kinetic energy of liberated electrons of M<sub>A</sub> : M<sub>B</sub> is in the ratio of 2.642 : 1. The work function (in eV) of M<sub>A</sub> and M<sub>B</sub> are respectively.
steps: Let φ<sub>A</sub> = φ, φ<sub>B</sub> = 2φ. Then KE<sub>A</sub> = 6 − φ and KE<sub>B</sub> = 6 − 2φ.
(6 − φ)/(6 − 2φ) = 2.642 ⇒ 6 − φ = 15.852 − 5.284φ ⇒ 4.284φ = 9.852 ⇒ φ ≈ 2.3 eV.
So φ<sub>A</sub> = 2.3 eV and φ<sub>B</sub> = 4.6 eV (KE = 3.7 and 1.4 eV, ratio 2.64).

qs.stem:
Identify the INCORRECT statements from the following :
A. Notation 2412Mg represents 24 protons and 12 neutrons.
B. Wavelength of a radiation of frequency 4.5 × 1015 s−1 is 6.7 × 10−8 m.
C. One radiation has wavelength = λ1 (900 nm) and energy = E1. Other radiation has wavelength = λ2 (300 nm) and energy = E2. E1 : E2 = 3 : 1.
D. Number of photons of light of wavelength 2000 pm that provides 1 J of energy is 1.006 × 1016.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: A: in <sup>24</sup><sub>12</sub>Mg, 24 is the mass number and 12 the proton number (12 neutrons), so A is incorrect.
B: λ = c/ν = 3 × 10<sup>8</sup>/4.5 × 10<sup>15</sup> = 6.7 × 10<sup>−8</sup> m, correct. C: E ∝ 1/λ, so E<sub>1</sub>:E<sub>2</sub> = 300:900 = 1:3, so C is incorrect.
D: n = Eλ/(hc) = (1 × 2 × 10<sup>−9</sup>)/(6.626 × 10<sup>−34</sup> × 3 × 10<sup>8</sup>) ≈ 1.006 × 10<sup>16</sup>, correct. Incorrect: A and C.

qs.stem:
Which of the following statements are TRUE about Haloform reaction ?
A. Sodium hypochlorite reacts with KI to give KOI.
B. KOI is a reducing agent.
C. α, β–unsaturated methylketone (CH3–CH=CH–CO–CH3) will give iodoform reaction.
D. Isopropyl alcohol will not give iodoform test.
E. Methanoic acid will give positive iodoform test.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: A: NaOCl + KI → KOI + NaCl, true. B: hypoiodite is an oxidising (halogenating) agent, so false.

C: CH<sub>3</sub>CH=CHCOCH<sub>3</sub> has a CH<sub>3</sub>CO– group, so it gives the test: true. D: isopropyl alcohol has CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)–, oxidised to a methyl ketone, so it does give the test: false.
E: HCOOH has no CH<sub>3</sub>CO or CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH) unit, so false. True: A and C.

qs.stem: A student has been given a compound 'x' of molecular formula C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>7</sub>N. 'x' is sparingly soluble in water. However, on addition of dilute mineral acid, 'x' becomes soluble in water. 'x' when treated with CHCl<sub>3</sub> and KOH (alc.), 'y' is produced. 'y' has a specific unpleasant smell. On treatment with benzenesulphonyl chloride, 'x' gives a compound 'z' which is soluble in alkali. The number of different 'H' atoms present in 'z' is :-
steps: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>7</sub>N basic and giving the carbylamine test (foul-smelling isocyanide) means x = aniline, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>NH<sub>2</sub>.
Hinsberg reagent with a primary amine gives z = C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>NHSO<sub>2</sub>C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub> (alkali soluble, since N–H is acidic).
Distinct H: ortho, meta, para on each ring (3 + 3 = 6) plus the N–H = 7.

qs.stem:
Iodoform test can differentiate between
A. Methanol and Ethanol
B. CH3COOH and CH3CH2COOH
C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone
D. Diethyl ether and Pentan–3–one
E. Anisole and acetone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: The test is positive for CH<sub>3</sub>CO– and CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)– units, including ethanol (CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH).
A: methanol negative, ethanol positive, so they are distinguished. E: anisole negative, acetone positive, distinguished.
B (both acids), C (cyclohexanone has no CH<sub>3</sub>CO), D (pentan-3-one is not a methyl ketone) give the same result for both members. Answer: A and E only.

qs.stem: In Carius method 0.2425 g of an organic compound gave 0.5253 g silver chloride. The percentage of chlorine in the organic compound is

Given below are two statements :
Statement I : (CH3)3C+ is more stable than CH3+ as nine hyperconjugation interactions are possible in (CH3)3C+.
Statement II : CH3+ is less stable than (CH3)3C+ as only three hyperconjugation interactions are possible in CH3+.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: (CH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>C<sup>+</sup> has 9 α-C–H bonds adjacent to the cationic carbon, so nine hyperconjugation structures; it is more stable. Statement I is true.
CH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup> has no α-carbon bearing hydrogens, so it has no hyperconjugation at all; the claim of three interactions is false. Statement II is false.
opts: Statement I is true but statement II is false.
Statement I is false but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Both statement I and Statement II are true.

qs.stem:
Observe the following reactions at T(K).
I. A → products
II. 5Br−(aq) + BrO3−(aq) + 6H+(aq) → 3Br2(aq) + 3H2O(l)
Both the reactions are started at 10.00 am. The rates of these reactions at 10.10 am are same. The value of −Δ[Br−]/Δt at 10.10 am is 2 × 10−4 mol L−1 min−1. The concentration of A at 10.10 am is 10−2 mol L−1. What is the first order rate constant (in min−1) of reaction I ?
steps: Rate of reaction II = (1/5)(−Δ[Br<sup>−</sup>]/Δt) = (2 × 10<sup>−4</sup>)/5 = 4 × 10<sup>−5</sup> mol L<sup>−1</sup> min<sup>−1</sup>.
Rate of reaction I is the same: k[A] = 4 × 10<sup>−5</sup> with [A] = 10<sup>−2</sup>.
k = 4 × 10<sup>−5</sup>/10<sup>−2</sup> = 4 × 10<sup>−3</sup> min<sup>−1</sup>.

qs.stem: 200 cc of x × 10<sup>−3</sup> M potassium dichromate is required to oxidise 750 cc of 0.6 M Mohr's salt solution in acidic medium. Here x = _______ .
steps: Moles of Fe<sup>2+</sup> = 0.750 L × 0.6 M = 0.45 mol. Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sup>2−</sup> + 6Fe<sup>2+</sup> + 14H<sup>+</sup> → 2Cr<sup>3+</sup> + 6Fe<sup>3+</sup> + 7H<sub>2</sub>O.
Moles of dichromate = 0.45/6 = 0.075 mol (75 mmol) in 0.200 L, so M = 0.375 M.
x × 10<sup>−3</sup> = 0.375, so x = 375.

qs.stem: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At 320 K, the vapour pressure for the solution, containing 3 mol of A and 1 mol of B is 500 mm Hg. At the same temperature, if 1 mol of A is further added to this solution, vapour pressure of the solution increases by 20 mm Hg. Vapour pressure (in mm Hg) of B in pure state is ______ . (Nearest integer)
steps: First case (x<sub>A</sub> = 3/4, x<sub>B</sub> = 1/4): 3P<sub>A</sub>° + P<sub>B</sub>° = 2000.
Second case (4 mol A, 1 mol B, total 520 mm): 4P<sub>A</sub>° + P<sub>B</sub>° = 2600.
Subtracting: P<sub>A</sub>° = 600, then P<sub>B</sub>° = 2000 − 1800 = 200 mm Hg.

qs.stem: Total number of unpaired electrons present in the central metal atoms/ions of [Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub>], [NiCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>, [PtCl<sub>2</sub>(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>], [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> and [Pt(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> is ________ .
steps: [Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub>]: Ni(0) 3d<sup>10</sup>, 0 unpaired. [NiCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>: Ni<sup>2+</sup> d<sup>8</sup> with weak Cl<sup>−</sup>, tetrahedral sp<sup>3</sup>, 2 unpaired.

[PtCl<sub>2</sub>(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>]: Pt<sup>2+</sup> 5d<sup>8</sup>, square planar (5d strong field), 0 unpaired. [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>: strong CN<sup>−</sup> pairs the d<sup>8</sup> electrons, square planar, 0. [Pt(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>: 0.
Total = 2.

qs.stem:
Consider the following reaction of benzene.
Benzene + H3C–CO–CH2–CH2–CO–Cl → (P) (anhydrous AlCl3), then (P) → (Q) (aq. NaOH, Δ).
In compound (Q), the percentage of oxygen is ________ %. (Nearest integer)
steps: Friedel–Crafts acylation at the acid chloride gives P = C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>CO–CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CO–CH<sub>3</sub> (a 1,4-diketone).
With aq. NaOH, the CH<sub>3</sub> carbanion attacks the aryl ketone (intramolecular aldol), and heating dehydrates it to 3-phenylcyclopent-2-en-1-one, C<sub>11</sub>H<sub>10</sub>O, M = 158.

qs.stem:
X2(g) + Y2(g) ⇌ 2Z(g)
X2(g) and Y2(g) are added to a 1 L flask and it is found that the system attains the above equilibrium at T(K) with the number of moles of X2(g), Y2(g) and Z(g) being 3, 3 and 9 mol respectively (equilibrium moles). Under this condition of equilibrium, 10 mol of Z(g) is added to the flask and the temperature is maintained at T(K). Then the number of moles of Z(g) in the flask when the new equilibrium is established is ______ . (Nearest integer)
steps: K<sub>c</sub> = 9<sup>2</sup>/(3 × 3) = 9 (volume 1 L).
After adding 10 mol Z: [Z] = 19, Q = 19<sup>2</sup>/9 > K<sub>c</sub>, so the reaction shifts backward. At new equilibrium: X<sub>2</sub> = Y<sub>2</sub> = 3 + a, Z = 19 − 2a.
(19 − 2a)/(3 + a) = 3 ⇒ 19 − 2a = 9 + 3a ⇒ a = 2, so Z = 19 − 4 = 15 mol.

Numerical answers match the NTA final key (16 Feb 2026); lettered answers follow the printed official answer and were each re-solved independently.
